correction.text: Eritrea within its present borders from 24 May 1991 ('De facto: 24 May 1991'): Cliopatria's 1992 shape, unchanged, drawn one year earlier

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins the State of Eritrea in 1992, but the infobox gives de facto independence on 24 May 1991 and 'the Eritrean War of Independence went on for 30 years against successive Ethiopian governments until 1991'. The EPLF dossier already hands the whole country to this state in May 1991.

126,704 km2 against the infobox 120,000 km2 (and 'approximately 117,600 km2' in the lead): ratio 1.06-1.08, fine. The outline stands for 1992-2023 as the state's own land; Ethiopian-held Badme (1999 to 2020) and the war's contested fronts are drawn by the ledger's occupation and contest events, not by changing the shape.
Identical to the 1992 shape; no territorial change in 2024 is recorded on the page.

ledger.note: 1991: Eritrea becomes independent in fact after thirty years of war. Infobox 'Independence from Ethiopia: De facto: 24 May 1991; De jure: 24 May 1993'; 'the Eritrean People's Liberation Front (EPLF), a successor of the ELF, defeated the Ethiopian forces in Eritrea'; the war 'went on for 30 years ... until 1991'. The 1993 referendum is not dated on the page; UN admission was 28 May 1993.

region.text: the Badme region, entered by 'a large Eritrean mechanized force' on 6 May 1998

ledger.note: 1998: Eritrean and Ethiopian troops fight over Badme. 'On 6 May 1998 ... a large Eritrean mechanized force entered the Badme region' after firefights with a Tigrayan militia and Ethiopian police; Ethiopia's parliament declared war on 13 May. 'Accounts differ on who initiated the conflict.'

1999: Ethiopia retakes Badme. 'On 22 February 1999, Ethiopia launched a massive military offensive to recapture Badme'; the infobox says 'Ethiopian occupation of disputed territories and the border town of Badme until the 2020 Tigray War'. The 14 April 2002 commission ruling 'awarded some territory to each side, but Badme ... was awarded to Eritrea', so the Ethiopian presence is an occupation of Eritrean land from then at the latest. Dated to match the Ethiopia dossier's occupation_start.

region.text: the Tsorona front, where Ethiopian forces attacked on 16 March 1999

ledger.note: 1999: the fighting spreads to the Tsorona front. 'On 16 March, following a two-week lull, Ethiopian forces launched an offensive on the Tsorona front.'

region.text: Barentu and the Western front, 'taken in a surprise Ethiopian pincer movement' in May 2000

ledger.note: 2000: Ethiopia's offensive takes the Western front. 'Barentu was taken in a surprise Ethiopian pincer movement on the Western front'; Ethiopia 'declared the war was over on 25 May 2000'. The page gives no day for Barentu and does not say when the Ethiopian forces left.

region.text: the border town of Zalambessa, from which 'the Eritreans claimed they withdrew' in May 2000

ledger.note: 2000: Zalambessa is given up. Ethiopia claimed to have taken it; 'the Eritreans claimed they withdrew from the disputed border town of Zalambessa and other disputed areas'.

region.text: the Badme region, entered by 'a large Eritrean mechanized force' on 6 May 1998

ledger.note: 2000: the Algiers peace ends the fighting over Badme. 'On 12 December 2000 a peace agreement was signed by the two governments'; a 25 km-wide Temporary Security Zone 'within Eritrea' was set up on 31 July 2000 under UNMEE. The Ethiopian occupation of Badme continues (see occupation_end 2020). Dated to match the Ethiopia dossier.

region.text: the Tsorona front, where Ethiopian forces attacked on 16 March 1999

ledger.note: 2000: the Algiers peace ends the fighting on the Tsorona front. 'On 12 December 2000 a peace agreement was signed by the two governments.' The last battles were in May 2000 (Ethiopia 'declared the war was over on 25 May 2000').

region.text: Barentu and the Western front, 'taken in a surprise Ethiopian pincer movement' in May 2000

ledger.note: 2000: the Algiers peace ends the fighting on the Western front. 'On 12 December 2000 a peace agreement was signed by the two governments.' The page does not say when Ethiopian troops left Barentu.

region.text: the border town of Zalambessa, from which 'the Eritreans claimed they withdrew' in May 2000

ledger.note: 2000: the Algiers peace closes the Zalambessa front. 'On 12 December 2000 a peace agreement was signed by the two governments.'

2020: Ethiopia's hold on Badme ends. Infobox 'Ethiopian occupation of disputed territories and the border town of Badme until the 2020 Tigray War'; the page also has 'On 5 June 2018 ... agreed to fully implement the peace treaty signed with Eritrea in 2000' and 'peace declared by both parties in July 2018' but no handover date. The Eritrea page says the border conflict 'was not resolved until 2018'.

wars.name: Eritrean-Ethiopian War

zones.text: the Badme region, entered by 'a large Eritrean mechanized force' on 6 May 1998
the Tsorona front, where Ethiopian forces attacked on 16 March 1999
Barentu and the Western front, 'taken in a surprise Ethiopian pincer movement' in May 2000
the border town of Zalambessa, from which 'the Eritreans claimed they withdrew' in May 2000

wars.outcome: Fighting ended with the 12 December 2000 Algiers peace agreement; on 14 April 2002 the boundary commission's 'final and binding' ruling awarded Badme to Eritrea, but Ethiopian forces held it until 2020. The infobox calls it an 'Ethiopian military victory' and an 'Eritrean diplomatic victory'.
wars.note: Front by year: Badme region 6 May 1998; Ethiopian recapture offensive 22 February 1999; Tsorona 16 March 1999; Barentu and Zalambessa May 2000. The page gives no clear map of who held which town between those dates, so the zones are the places it names with a radius.

wars.name: Tigray War
wars.outcome: 'In 2020, Eritrean troops intervened in the Tigray War on the side of the Ethiopian government'; 'In April 2021, Eritrea confirmed its troops were fighting in Ethiopia'. The Eritrea page names no land held and no withdrawal.
wars.note: End year 2022 set by the reviewer from the Tigray War page ('lasted from 3 November 2020 to 3 November 2022'; cessation of hostilities 2 November 2022, to which 'Eritrea was not a party'); the Eritrean-held band of Tigray is in the Ethiopia dossier, which records the occupation from its side.

certainty.note: Undelimited frontier with Ethiopia (the Badme conflict 'was not resolved until 2018'); the Red Sea islands (Hanish, Doumeira) are disputed with Yemen and Djibouti.

The 14 April 2002 commission ruling is 'final and binding' on the Ethiopian frontier, though Ethiopia held Badme to 2020 and the page records no demarcation; the Djibouti and Yemen frontiers stay tense ('territorial disputes over the Doumeira Islands and Hanish Islands').

notes: Page budget 1-2: both pages opened. (1) Cliopatria starts the State of Eritrea in 1992; this dossier starts in May 1991 (de facto, per the infobox) with a new keyframe for 1991, matching the EPLF and Ethiopia dossiers. The 1993 referendum is not dated on the page. (2) Ethiopia's dossier records the Badme occupation from 1999-02 to 2020 and the contest from 1998-05 to 2000-12 with a border band; this dossier mirrors those dates with the page's named places as zones. (3) The Eritrea page is silent on the 1995-1996 Hanish Islands fighting with Yemen, the 1998 arbitration and the 2008 Djibouti clash; none was opened (page budget), so Eritrea's Red Sea frontiers have no contest or loss event and the Cliopatria outline (126,704 km2 against 120,000 km2) is kept. (4) The page gives no land for Eritrean troops in Tigray; the Ethiopia dossier holds that occupation. (5) Gazetteer lacks Badme, Zalambessa, Tsorona and Barentu (used as place names). (6) The 2002 boundary decision is not a ledger event (it would be a gain of a land already held by Ethiopia); it is recorded in the Badme occupation note and the war outcome.
